readings.title: A Plea from Desolation
readings.subtitle: Where is Your ardor and compassion?
readings.text: [Isaiah 63:15] Look down from the heavens, and see from <dn>Your</dn> set-apart and comely dwelling. Where are <dn>Your</dn> ardour and <dn>Your</dn> might, the stirring of <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> inward parts and <dn>Your</dn> compassion toward me? Are they withheld? [16] For <dn>You</dn> are our Father, though Aḇraham does not know us, and Yisra’ěl does not recognise us. <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, are our Father, our Redeemer – <dn>Your</dn> Name is from of old. [17] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, why do <dn>You</dn> make us stray from <dn>Your</dn> ways, and harden our heart from <dn>Your</dn> fear? Turn back, for the sake of <dn>Your</dn> servants, the tribes of <dn>Your</dn> inheritance. [18] For a little while <dn>Your</dn> set-apart people possessed it – our adversaries have trodden down <dn>Your</dn> set-apart place. [19] We have become like those over whom <dn>You</dn> never ruled – <dn>Your</dn> Name is not called on them!

readings.title: Oh, That You Would Rend the Heavens
readings.subtitle: We have all become as one unclean.
readings.text: [Isaiah 64:1] Oh, that <dn>You</dn> would tear the heavens open, come down, that mountains shall shake before <dn>You</dn> – [2] as when fire burns twigs, as fire makes water boil – to make <dn>Your</dn> Name known to <dn>Your</dn> adversaries, so that nations tremble before <dn>You</dn>. [3] When <dn>You</dn> did awesome matters, which we did not expect, <dn>You</dn> came down, mountains did shake before <dn>You</dn>! [4] Since the beginning of the ages they have not heard nor perceived by the ear, nor has the eye seen any <dn>Elohim</dn> besides <dn>You</dn>, who acts for those who wait for <dn>Him</dn>. [5] <dn>You</dn> shall meet him who rejoices and does righteousness, who remembers <dn>You</dn> in <dn>Your</dn> ways. See, <dn>You</dn> were wroth when we sinned in them a long time. And should we be saved? [6] And all of us have become as one unclean, and all our righteousnesses are as soiled rags. And all of us fade like a leaf, and our crookednesses, like the wind, have taken us away. [7] And there is no one who calls on <dn>Your</dn> Name, who stirs himself up to be strengthened in <dn>You</dn>; for <dn>You</dn> have hidden <dn>Your</dn> face from us, and have consumed us because of our crookednesses.

readings.title: You Are Our Father
readings.subtitle: Would You restrain Yourself, O YeHoVaH?
readings.text: [Isaiah 64:8] And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> are our Father. We are the clay, and <dn>You</dn> our potter. And we are all the work of <dn>Your</dn> hand. [9] Do not be wroth, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor remember crookedness forever. See, please look, all of us are <dn>Your</dn> people! [10] <dn>Your</dn> set-apart cities have become a wilderness, Tsiyon has become a wilderness, Yerushalayim a waste. [11] Our set-apart and comely House, where our fathers praised <dn>You</dn>, has been burned up with fire. And all that we treasured has become a ruin. [12] In view of all this, would <dn>You</dn> restrain <dn>Yourself</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? Would <dn>You</dn> keep silent and afflict us beyond measure?

readings.subsection: The Divine Response and Final Judgment
readings.title: The Rebellious People
readings.subtitle: I have held out My hands all day long.
readings.text: [Isaiah 65:1] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have let <dn>Myself</dn> be inquired of, not by those who asked; <dn>I</dn> was found, not by those who sought <dn>Me</dn>. <dn>I</dn> said, ‘Here <dn>I</dn> am, here <dn>I</dn> am,’ to a nation not calling on <dn>My</dn> Name.</dq> [2] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have held out <dn>My</dn> hands all day long to a stubborn people, who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts;</dq> [3] <dq>the people who provoke <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn> continually to <dn>My</dn> face, who slaughter in gardens, and burn incense on slaughter-places of brick;</dq> [4] <dq>who sit among the burial-sites, and spend the night in secret places, who eat flesh of pigs, and the broth of unclean meat is in their pots,</dq> [5] <dq>who say, ‘Keep to yourself, do not come near me, for <dn>I</dn> am set-apart to you!’ These are smoke in <dn>My</dn> nostrils, a fire that burns all day.</dq> [6] <dq>“See, it is written before <dn>Me</dn>: <dn>I</dn> am not silent, but shall repay, and <dn>I</dn> shall repay into their bosom,</dq> [7] <dq>your crookednesses and the crookednesses of your fathers together,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“who burned incense on the mountains and reproached <dn>Me</dn> on the hills. And <dn>I</dn> shall measure their former work into their bosom.”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Divine Response and Final Judgment
readings.title: A Remnant Shall Be Saved
readings.subtitle: I shall allot you to the sword.
readings.text: [Isaiah 65:8] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one shall say, ‘Do not destroy it, for there is blessing in it,’ so <dn>I</dn> do for <dn>My</dn> servants’ sake, not to destroy them all.</dq> [9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall bring forth a seed from Ya‛aqoḇ, and from Yehuḏah an heir of <dn>My</dn> mountains. And <dn>My</dn> chosen ones shall inherit it, and <dn>My</dn> servants dwell there.</dq> [10] <dq>“And Sharon shall be a fold of flocks, and the Valley of Aḵor a place for herds to lie down, for <dn>My</dn> people who have sought <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [11] <dq>“But you are those who forsake <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who forget <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> set-apart mountain, who prepare a table for Gad, and who fill a drink offering for Meni.</dq> [12] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall allot you to the sword, and let you all bow down to the slaughter, because <dn>I</dn> called and you did not answer, <dn>I</dn> spoke and you did not hear, and you did evil before <dn>My</dn> eyes and chose that in which <dn>I</dn> did not delight.”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Divine Response and Final Judgment
readings.title: The Two Fates
readings.subtitle: My servants shall eat, but you shall hunger.
readings.text: [Isaiah 65:13] Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>My</dn> servants eat, but you hunger; see, <dn>My</dn> servants drink, but you thirst; see, <dn>My</dn> servants rejoice, but you are put to shame;</dq> [14] <dq>see, <dn>My</dn> servants sing for joy of heart, but you cry for sorrow of heart, and wail for breaking of spirit.</dq> [15] <dq>“And you shall leave your name as a curse to <dn>My</dn> chosen, for the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall put you to death, and call <dn>His</dn> servants by another name,</dq> [16] <dq>so that he who blesses himself in the earth does bless himself in the <dn>Elohim</dn> of truth. And he who swears in the earth does swear by the <dn>Elohim</dn> of truth. Because the former distresses shall be forgotten, and because they shall be hidden from <dn>My</dn> eyes.</dq>

readings.subsection: The Divine Response and Final Judgment
readings.title: New Heavens and a New Earth
readings.subtitle: The former shall not be remembered.
readings.text: [Isaiah 65:17] <dq>“For look, <dn>I</dn> am creating new heavens and <dn>את</dn> a new earth, and the former shall not be remembered, nor come to heart.</dq> [18] <dq>“But be glad and rejoice forever in what <dn>I</dn> create; for look, <dn>I</dn> create <dn>את</dn> Yerushalayim a rejoicing, and her people a joy.</dq> [19] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall rejoice in Yerushalayim, and shall joy in <dn>My</dn> people, and let the voice of weeping no more be heard in her, nor the voice of crying.</dq> [20] <dq>“No more is an infant from there going to live but a few days, nor an old man who does not complete <dn>את</dn> his days, for the youth dies one hundred years old, but the sinner being one hundred years old shall be lightly esteemed.</dq> [21] <dq>“And they shall build houses and inhabit them, and plant vineyards and eat <dn>את</dn> their fruit.</dq> [22] <dq>“They shall not build and another inhabit; they shall not plant and another eat. For the days of <dn>My</dn> people are going to be as the days of a tree, and <dn>My</dn> chosen ones outlive the work of their hands.</dq> [23] <dq>“They shall not labour in vain, nor bring forth children for trouble. For they are the seed of the blessed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and their offspring with them.</dq> [24] <dq>“And it shall be that before they call, <dn>I</dn> answer. And while they are still speaking, <dn>I</dn> hear.</dq> [25] <dq>“Wolf and lamb feed together, a lion eats straw as an ox, and dust is the snake’s food. They shall do no evil, nor destroy in all <dn>My</dn> set-apart mountain,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.subsection: The Divine Response and Final Judgment
readings.title: The True Dwelling Place
readings.subtitle: To this one I look: on him who is poor and bruised of spirit.
readings.text: [Isaiah 66:1] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“The heavens are <dn>My</dn> throne, and the earth is <dn>My</dn> footstool. Where is this house that you build for <dn>Me</dn>? And where is this place of <dn>My</dn> rest?</dq> [2] <dq>“And <dn>את</dn> all these <dn>My</dn> hand has made, and all these that exist,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“Yet to such a one <dn>I</dn> look: on him who is poor and bruised of spirit, and who trembles at <dn>My</dn> Word.</dq> [3] <dq>“But whoever slays the bull strikes a man; whoever slaughters the lamb breaks a dog’s neck; whoever brings a grain offering – pig’s blood; whoever burns incense blesses an idol. Indeed, they have chosen their own ways, and their being delights in their abominations.</dq> [4] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall also choose their punishments, and bring their fears on them. Because <dn>I</dn> called, but no one answered. <dn>I</dn> spoke and they did not hear, and they did evil before <dn>My</dn> eyes, and chose what was displeasing to <dn>Me</dn>.”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Divine Response and Final Judgment
readings.title: Zion's Sudden Birth
readings.subtitle: Rejoice with Yerushalayim.
readings.text: [Isaiah 66:5] Hear the Word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, you who tremble at <dn>His</dn> Word, <dq>“<dn>Your</dn> brothers who hate you, who cast you out for <dn>My</dn> Name’s sake, said, ‘Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be esteemed, so that we see your joy.’ But they are put to shame.”</dq> [6] <dq>“A roaring sound from the city, a voice from the Hěḵal, the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, repaying <dn>His</dn> enemies!</dq> [7] <dq>“Before she laboured, she gave birth; before a pain came to her, she was delivered of a male child.</dq> [8] <dq>“Who has heard the like of this? Who has seen the like of these? Is a land brought forth in one day? Is a nation born at once? For as soon as Tsiyon laboured, she gave birth to her children.</dq> [9] <dq>“Shall <dn>I</dn> bring to birth, and not give delivery?”</dq> says <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“Shall <dn>I</dn> who give delivery restrain birth?”</dq> said your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [10] “Rejoice with Yerushalayim, and be glad with her, all you who love her; rejoice greatly with her, all you who mourn for her; [11] so that you feed, and shall be satisfied with the breast of her comforts, so that you drink deeply, and shall delight yourselves in her overflowing esteem.” [12] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am extending peace to her like a river, and the esteem of the nations like a flowing stream. And you shall feed; you shall be carried on the side, and be fondled on her knees.</dq> [13] <dq>“As one whom his mother comforts, so <dn>I</dn> comfort you. And in Yerushalayim you are comforted.”</dq> [14] “And you shall see, and your heart shall rejoice, and your bones flourish as tender grass. And the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be known to <dn>His</dn> servants, and <dn>His</dn> displeasure to <dn>His</dn> enemies.

readings.subsection: The Divine Response and Final Judgment
readings.title: The Final Judgment
readings.subtitle: By fire and by His sword YeHoVaH shall judge all flesh.
readings.text: [Isaiah 66:15] “For look, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> comes with fire and with <dn>His</dn> chariots, like a whirlwind, to render <dn>His</dn> displeasure with burning, and <dn>His</dn> rebuke with flames of fire. [16] “For by fire and by <dn>His</dn> sword <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall judge <dn>את</dn> all flesh, and the slain of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be many – [17] those who set themselves apart and cleanse themselves at the gardens after ‘one’ in the midst, eating flesh of pigs and the abomination and the mouse, are snatched away, together,” declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [18] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn>, because of their works and their imaginations, am coming to gather <dn>את</dn> all nations and tongues. And they shall come and see <dn>My</dn> esteem.</dq> [19] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall set a sign among them, and shall send some of those who escape to the nations – Tarshish and Pul and Luḏ, who draw the bow, and Tuḇal and Yavan, the coastlands afar off who have not heard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> report nor seen <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> esteem. And they shall declare <dn>My</dn> esteem among the nations.</dq> [20] <dq>“And they shall bring <dn>את</dn> all your brothers as an offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> out of all the nations, on horses and in chariots and in litters, on mules and on camels, to <dn>My</dn> set-apart mountain Yerushalayim,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“as the children of Yisra’ěl bring <dn>את</dn> an offering in a clean vessel into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [21] <dq>“And from them too <dn>I</dn> shall take for priests – for Lěvites,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.subsection: The Divine Response and Final Judgment
readings.title: The Everlasting Kingdom
readings.subtitle: From New moon to New moon, all flesh shall come to worship before Me.
readings.text: [Isaiah 66:22] <dq>“For as the new heavens and the new earth that <dn>I</dn> make stand before <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“so your seed and your name shall stand.</dq> [23] <dq>“And it shall be that from New moon to New moon, and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh shall come to worship before <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [24] <dq>“And they shall go forth and look upon the corpses of the men who have transgressed against <dn>Me</dn>. For their worm shall not die, and their fire not be quenched. And they shall be repulsive to all flesh!”</dq>

readings.title: The Annals of Hezekiah
readings.subtitle: He slept with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigned.
readings.text: [2 Kings 20:20] And the rest of the acts of Ḥizqiyahu, and all his might and how he made <dn>את</dn> a pool and <dn>את</dn> a channel and brought <dn>את</dn> water into the city, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? [21] So Ḥizqiyahu slept with his fathers. And Menashsheh his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: The Legacy of Hezekiah
readings.subtitle: Written in the vision of Yeshayahu the prophet.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 32:32] Now the rest of the acts of Ḥizqiyahu, and his goodness, see, they are written in the vision of Yeshayahu the prophet, son of Amots, and in the book of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah and Yisra’ěl. [33] So Ḥizqiyahu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the upper part of the tombs of the sons of Daviḏ. And all Yehuḏah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim did him honour at his death. And Menashsheh his son reigned in his place.
